fields.name: Base - work income (natural persons)

report_evidence.column: W - WITHOLDING TAX BASIS WITHOUT CONTRIBUTION

fields.finding: WHAT MATCHES: column U 'WITHOLDING TAX BASIS' is the DEPURATED base the spec describes, and it is the base paired with the withholding actually practised (V): for Procedure 2, V = U x '% Retention' on 96 of 103 employees. The client's depuration, verified on all 261 employees, is: Income Total (G = basic/integral salary E + other income F) less mandatory EPS/AFP/FSP contributions (H) less TOTAL TAX RELIEF (S), where S = min(AFC I + APV J + dependants L + prepaid medicine M + housing interest N + 25% exempt income P; 40% of (G - H) [column R]; 5,848,430 = 1,340 UVT / 12 at UVT 52,374). U = G - H - S holds for 256 of 261; for 5 employees U = G - H (no relief applied, reason not visible in the report). The spec text omits AFC/APV and the 40% / 1,340 UVT cap. CONFLICT: 7 employees with Master Data 'Tax Procedure 1' = 3 carry % Retention 0.2 and a withholding of exactly 20% of GROSS Income Total G (e.g. G 245,443,528 -> V 49,088,706; this is the ET art. 408 pattern), yet the client's base column U shows a DEPURATED value for them (237,618,312). The spec states that for a non-resident taxed under art. 408 the base is the GROSS. Summing U, as the client report does, therefore contradicts the spec rule for these employees. In addition the spec itself routes non-resident employees both to casilla 77 (this row: 'for a NON-RESIDENT taxed under art. 408 the base is the GROSS') and to casillas 109/110 via sheet 2 (rows 31/33: 'THE NON-RESIDENT EMPLOYEE BASE CASILLA'); the client report shows no sheet-2 / treaty / country split at all. Second open point: the client also keeps an alternative base W 'WITHOLDING TAX BASIS WITHOUT CONTRIBUTION' (populated for 133 of 261, total 4,000,634,596 vs U 6,263,719,152); only U pairs with the withholding deducted, but which base is declared must be confirmed. Rounding: client per-employee and GRAND TOTAL values are whole pesos (no decimals in any of columns U-Y); this is consistent with the spec, provided the nearest-1,000 rounding is applied once to the monthly casilla total, not per employee.
fields.proposed_explanation: Sum, over every employee paid in the month (all payroll runs of the entity, not one run), of the DEPURATED monthly withholding base of ET art. 388 for residents: gross work income (basic or integral salary plus all other taxable income) LESS mandatory employee contributions to EPS, AFP and the Solidarity/Subsistence fund (non-constitutive income), LESS the total tax relief, where total tax relief = AFC/AVC contributions + voluntary pension contributions + dependants deduction (10% of gross income, max 32 UVT) + prepaid medicine + housing-loan interest + 25% exempt income (max 790 UVT annual / 12), capped at the lower of 40% of (gross income less mandatory contributions) and 1,340 UVT annual / 12. In the client's Base of Withholding this is column U 'WITHOLDING TAX BASIS' (not column W). [DECISION PENDING - see Query to RA] Employees taxed under ET art. 408 as non-residents (client Tax Procedure 3, rate 20%): their base is the GROSS work income (Base of Withholding column G 'Income Total'), not column U; confirm whether they are declared here or in casillas 109/110 via sheet 2. Also sweeps in fees paid to natural persons under the art. 383 table, which payroll does not supply. Rounding: keep per-employee bases in whole pesos; round only the monthly aggregate to the nearest 1,000.
fields.official_source: ET art. 388 (depurated withholding base), ET art. 387 (dependants, prepaid medicine, housing interest), ET art. 206 num. 10 (25% exempt income), ET art. 126-1 / 126-4 (AFC/AVC/voluntary pension), ET art. 336 (40% / 1,340 UVT annual cap on exempt income and deductions) - as cited by the spec (art. 388/387/25%) or to be confirmed by the RA (art. 336 cap, art. 126-1/126-4); ET art. 408 (non-resident 20% on gross), as cited in the spec

fields.name: Withholding - work income (natural persons)

report_evidence.example_masked: Sep total 1543834892 (of which 144635503 for 97 IDs outside the Base of Withholding run)

fields.finding: WHAT THE CLIENT DATA SHOWS: (1) Of the two withholding columns, V 'WITH CONTRIBUTION' is the one actually deducted: the per-employee G2N WT 2552 'Income Tax (employee)' deduction equals V for 255 of 261 employees, and the remaining 6 are employees where 2552 nets to zero as a non-cash item and the deduction is booked on WT 21330 'Personal Income Tax Withholding (Theoretical)' equal to V. Run total: 2552 (1,399,199,389) + 21330 (69,301,209) = 1,468,500,598 = GRAND TOTAL of V, exactly. (2) Y 'CONTINGENT WITHHOLDING' equals X - V on all 20 employees where Y > 0, and all 20 have AFC or APV contributions: it is the withholding NOT practised because of voluntary contributions; it is not deducted in the G2N (no WT carries it) and has no spec field. (3) The Base of Withholding is ONE payroll run (Payroll id REF-P201-065, generated 2026-09-16): the Accumulated Report shows 144,635,503 more of WT 2552 in Sep-2026 for 97 IDs outside that run, and other withholding WTs appear in other months (21129 Terminations, 25832 Stock awards vesting, 25833 'IC Local Country', 25834 'Hypothetical ... IC Foreign Country', 21140 Retirees). The spec explanation says only 'the month's total withholding' and the System Mapping 'SUM(Payroll.Income_Tax_Withheld)' does not tell the developer which WTs feed it, that all runs of the month are summed, or how contingent and theoretical/hypothetical tax are treated. (4) Rounding: client values are whole pesos; nearest-1,000 applies to the aggregate.
fields.proposed_explanation: THE PRINCIPAL PAYROLL CASILLA ON THE WITHHOLDING SIDE. Sum of the income-tax withholding at source actually practised on work income paid to natural persons in the calendar month, across EVERY payroll run of the entity in that month (regular, off-cycle and termination runs), in whole pesos, then rounded once to the nearest 1,000. Sources in the client's payroll: WT 2552 'Income Tax (employee)' (Deductions), plus, for tax-equalised employees where 2552 is booked as a net-zero non-cash item, WT 21330 'Personal Income Tax Withholding (Theoretical)' - together they reconcile to the Base of Withholding column V 'WITHOLDING TAX WITH CONTRIBUTION'. Do NOT use column X 'WITHOLDING TAX WITHOUT CONTRIBUTION'. [DECISION PENDING - see Query to RA] (a) whether CONTINGENT WITHHOLDING (column Y, = X - V, arising from AFC/voluntary-pension contributions) is excluded from this casilla; (b) whether withholding booked on WT 21129 (terminations), 25832 (stock-award vesting), 25833 and 25834 (IC local / hypothetical foreign) enters here in the month it is practised; (c) whether withholding on employees taxed under ET art. 408 (Tax Procedure 3) is reported here or in casillas 111/112. Must reconcile to the sum of RetencionFuente (NIE177) across every electronic payroll document of the same month. One of the casillas summed into casilla 130.
fields.official_source: ET art. 388 / 383 / 386 (withholding procedures), ET art. 126-1 and 126-4 (contingent withholding on AFC/voluntary pension, to be confirmed by RA), ET art. 577 (rounding), Res. DIAN 000013 de 2021 (NIE177), as cited in spec

fields.name: Base - pension income (natural persons)
fields.finding: The spec says this casilla is blank for an ordinary corporate payroll and that only the monthly pension EXCEEDING 1,000 UVT (52,374,000) is taxable. The client DOES pay retirees directly: Accumulated Report WT 62151 'Retirement Payment - PRV-6795' for 13 retirees in Sep-2026 (17 over the year), with income-tax withholding on WT 21140 every month (Oct-2025..Sep-2026 between 4,328,951 and 7,410,011). Every payment is far below 1,000 UVT (max 14,561,653), yet tax is withheld: the client applies the ET art. 383 table to 75% of the payment (e.g. 6,716,577 x 75% = 96.18 UVT -> 11,762; 11,868,537 -> 816,425), i.e. it treats the payment like work income with the 25% exemption, not as an art. 206 num. 5 exempt pension. This contradicts the spec's rule for casilla 78/94 OR shows these payments are not pensions under art. 206 num. 5 and belong in casillas 77/93. These retirees are not in the Base of Withholding, the Sep G2N or the Master Data (separate pay group), so whichever casilla applies, the Form 350 must aggregate this population too. Not decided here.
fields.official_source: ET art. 206 num. 5 (pension exemption up to 1,000 UVT monthly) as cited in the spec; ET art. 383 (table the client applies)

fields.name: Recipient country

report_evidence.example_masked: CO, co, CR, cr, CA, DO, CH, MX

fields.finding: The spec does not say which employee attribute supplies the country (System Mapping 'Employee.Treaty_Country_Code', shared with row 36). The only country data in the client reports is Master Data 'Country' (address country) and 'Nationality'. They name different countries for 15 employees (e.g. Nationality Argentina / Country MX; Nationality Colombia / Country DO), and 'Country' is held in mixed case ('co', 'cr' alongside 'CO', 'CR'). Of the 7 Procedure-3 (20%) employees, address countries are co, CR, DO, CH, co, CO, CO - so neither attribute reliably identifies a foreign tax residence. The developer needs to know the source and the normalisation.
fields.proposed_explanation: Country of TAX RESIDENCE of the non-resident payee (for a treaty claim, the country on the residence certificate), as an upper-case ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code. Do not derive it from Nationality. If the HR address country (Master Data 'Country') is used as a fallback it must be normalised to upper case (client data holds 'co', 'cr'). Where 'Treaty status' (casilla 141) = CON CONVENIO the country must be one with a treaty in force. Colombia's treaty network in force includes Spain, Chile, Switzerland, Canada, Mexico, South Korea, Portugal, India, the Czech Republic, the United Kingdom, France, Italy and Japan, plus Andean Community Decision 578.
fields.official_source: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2; Form 350 instruction guide sheet 2 (as cited in spec)
